feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 3 (±0.08 m, 0.016 m footprint, kp 6, kd 0.8) had zero line loss on the s-bend and slalom and oval steering_oscillation of 0.16, but all 60 trials ended off_track at max_error about 0.062. Progress was 0.18 on the s-bend and 0.09 on the slalom, and the oval finish rate fell to 45%, below iteration 2's 55%. Sensing coverage is now adequate, so the limit is the robot's turn response. I have adopted your narrower track and lighter, shorter body and kept the array fixed. Decide the next change from the race. If the s-bend or slalom still ends off_track with max_error at or near 0.06 m and progress below 0.3, the turn response is still too slow, so try wheel_track 0.09 m (within the 0.08 m limit) and keep mass at or below 0.7 kg. If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25 while max_error falls, the sensor lead is the suspect, so move sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03 with x fixed. If the oval finish rate drops below 55% with line loss still at zero, the extra turn authority is too high, so return wheel_track to 0.12 m and keep the shorter, lighter body.
requested_changes: If the s-bend or slalom still end off_track at max_error near 0.06 m with progress below 0.3, set wheel_track to 0.09 m and mass to 0.6 kg, keeping the ±0.08 m array fixed. Evidence: iteration 3 had zero line loss but max_error 0.062 and progress 0.18 and 0.09 on these tracks, so the limit is turn response.

If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, move every sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03, with x and the other fields fixed. Evidence: iteration 2 oval oscillation was 0.267 and iteration 1 was 0.275, both above the threshold, while iteration 3 was 0.16.

If the oval finish rate falls below 55% while line loss stays at zero, return wheel_track to 0.12 m and keep the shorter, lighter body. Evidence: iteration 2 reached 55% finish at track 0.12 m, and iteration 3 fell to 45% with the same track.
